[DDInter-0001 — Major Interaction] Ibuprofen inhibits platelet aggregation and causes gastrointestinal mucosal injury, synergistically increasing the risk of severe GI and systemic hemorrhage with warfarin. NSAIDs may also displace warfarin from plasma protein binding. Management: Avoid concomitant use. If analgesic/antipyretic therapy is needed, use acetaminophen (paracetamol) at the lowest effective dose and monitor INR closely.

[DDInter-0014 — Major Interaction] Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, blocking bioactivation of the prodrug clopidogrel to its active antiplatelet metabolite by ~40-50% and increasing stent thrombosis risk. Management: Avoid omeprazole and esomeprazole with clopidogrel. Switch gastroprotection to pantoprazole (minimal CYP2C19 inhibition) or famotidine.

[DDInter-0019 — Major Interaction] Additive potassium retention by lisinopril (ACE inhibitor) and spironolactone increases risk of severe hyperkalemia and cardiac arrhythmias, especially in CKD. Management: Keep spironolactone dose <=25-50 mg/day, monitor serum potassium and creatinine closely, and avoid potassium supplements.

[DDInter-0026 — Major Interaction] Clarithromycin potently inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism of simvastatin, causing up to 10-fold higher statin levels and severe rhabdomyolysis. Management: Contraindicated together. Temporarily suspend simvastatin during the course of clarithromycin, or use azithromycin instead.

[DDInter-0006 — Major Interaction] Metronidazole strongly inhibits CYP2C9-mediated metabolism of the more potent S-warfarin enantiomer, causing marked INR elevation and hemorrhage. Management: Avoid combination if possible. If co-prescribed, reduce warfarin dose by 25-40% and monitor INR every 2-3 days.
Exact Duplicate Ingredient (RxCUI ibuprofen): Brufen (400 mg TDS) and Advil (400 mg TDS) both contain 'ibuprofen'. Concurrent administration risks overdose and toxicity.

Same-Class Therapeutic Duplication (NSAID): Ibuprofen (ibuprofen, ATC: M01AE01), Diclofenac (diclofenac, ATC: M01AB05) belong to the same WHO/ISO ATC pharmacologic class (NSAID). Co-prescribing two drugs from the same class increases toxicity without added therapeutic benefit.
Direct Allergy Contraindication: Patient has a documented 'penicillin' allergy and 'Augmentin' (amoxicillin, ATC: J01CA04) belongs to the 'penicillin' group.

Cross-Reactivity Allergy Alert (penicillin -> cephalosporin): Penicillin to Cephalosporin cross-reactivity (~1-2% overall; higher with 1st-gen cephalexin sharing R1 side chain). Avoid cephalexin if index penicillin reaction was severe/anaphylaxis; use 3rd-gen ceftriaxone with caution if mild rash.

Cross-Reactivity Allergy Alert (aspirin -> cox2_nsaid): Aspirin-induced asthma/angioedema cross-reacts across all COX-1 NSAIDs (ibuprofen, diclofenac, naproxen, mefenamic acid) via leukotriene overproduction.
Maximum Daily Dose Exceeded: Prescribed Panadol equals 9000 mg/day (1500 mg × 6/day = 9000 mg/day), exceeding the maximum adult daily limit of 4000 mg/day.
Hepatic Dose Limit Exceeded: Calculated daily dose of Paracetamol (4000 mg/day) exceeds the maximum hepatic impairment limit of 2000 mg/day.

Renal Contraindication (Patient eGFR = 22.0 mL/min): KDIGO: CONTRAINDICATED if eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2 (lactic acidosis risk). If eGFR 30-44 mL/min, do not initiate or reduce maintenance dose to max 1000 mg/day.
